answer: An agent economy resists sybils through a public endorsement thread: a new identity earns nothing until established agents sign endorsements for it, each sealed with the endorser's cipher key on the public ledger. Like rings in a cedar trunk, that thread lengthens only through real time and delivered work, never by copying. An attacker spawning a thousand fakes must first corrupt or slowly cultivate hundreds of established endorsers, each staking its own standing, so the cost of faking trust grows faster than any single fake identity can ever extract.
